title: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships 2028/29
provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC)
summary: One-year taught master's study at a UK university for talented candidates from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries, including Pakistan. Applicants must be nominated by an approved national nominating body.
eligibleNationalities: Citizens of (or refugees in) eligible Commonwealth countries who are permanently resident there. Pakistan is listed as eligible.
eligibleDisciplines: Subjects relevant to the CSC's development themes; nominating bodies may set their own subject priorities.

coverage.tuition: Full tuition fees (paid directly to the university)
coverage.stipend: £1,712 per month, or £2,000 per month at universities in the London metropolitan area (rates quoted by CSC at current levels)
coverage.travel: Approved return airfare between home country and the UK
coverage.other: Study travel grant; child allowance for widowed, divorced or single-parent Scholars; needs assessment for disabled Scholars

eligibility: Be a citizen of, or have refugee status in, an eligible Commonwealth country, or be a British Protected Person
Be permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country
Be available to start UK study by September 2027
Be unable to afford UK study without the scholarship
Not have previously studied at master's level in the UK or held a Commonwealth Master's Scholarship
academicRequirements: By September 2027, a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours, or a lower second-class (2:2) degree plus a relevant postgraduate qualification.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027/28 deadline was 20 October 2026 (16:00 BST); the 2028/29 call has not been announced.

procedure: Check that your country and nominating body are eligible (in Pakistan, see the Higher Education Commission's Commonwealth Scholarship announcement).
Apply to your nominating body following its own rules and deadline.
Complete the CSC online application on the CSC application system before the CSC deadline.
Nominators forward shortlisted candidates to the CSC; the CSC makes the final selection.

verification.notes: Funding, eligibility and CSC deadline checked against the CSC's official page.

warnings: The CSC does not accept direct applications — you must also be nominated by an approved nominator.
Nominators often close earlier than the CSC deadline.

title: Chevening Scholarships 2028/29
provider: UK Government — Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)
summary: The UK government's global scholarship programme for future leaders, funding a one-year master's degree at a UK university. The 2027/28 application round has closed.
eligibleNationalities: Citizens of Chevening-eligible countries and territories (check the official country list).
eligibleDisciplines: Most taught master's subjects at eligible UK universities.

coverage.tuition: Full tuition (as described by the source checked)
coverage.stipend: Living expenses in the UK (monthly amount not specified by the source checked)

eligibility: Citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory
Meet Chevening's work-experience, education and return-home requirements as published for the cycle
Apply to eligible UK master's courses
academicRequirements: An undergraduate degree that enables entry to a UK postgraduate course (see official criteria).
languageRequirements: English requirements are set by the UK universities you apply to.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2027/28 deadline was 6 October 2026; the 2028/29 call has not been announced.

procedure: Read the eligibility criteria and country list on the official Chevening website.
Submit the online application during the annual window (usually August–October).
Shortlisted candidates are invited to interview at a British embassy or high commission.
Secure an unconditional offer from an eligible UK university before the official cut-off.

sources.label: Gdańsk University of Technology — Chevening 2027/28 notice

verification.notes: Deadline and coverage taken from a university notice and British Council page. Confirm details on chevening.org.

warnings: This round is closed. The next round has not been confirmed on this site yet.
Chevening scholars are normally expected to return to their home country after the award.

title: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship 2027
provider: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, managed by Campus France
summary: A French government award for outstanding international master's and PhD candidates. Students cannot apply directly — French higher-education institutions nominate their best applicants to Campus France.
eligibleNationalities: International (non-French) students; priority rules apply as set in the annual call.
eligibleDisciplines: Engineering and sciences; economics and management; law and political science (as defined in the annual call).

coverage.tuition: Not covered by the Eiffel allowance itself. Some institutions exempt laureates from fees (e.g. Université Paris Cité).
coverage.stipend: €1,200 per month (master's) / €2,000 per month (PhD), as published by Université Paris Cité for the 2027 call

eligibility: Master's: aged 29 or under (born after 31 March 1997) per the 2027 call as published by Université Paris Cité
PhD: aged 35 or under (born after 31 March 1991)
Must apply to a French institution, which then nominates candidates
academicRequirements: Excellent academic record; selection is by the nominating institution and then Campus France.
languageRequirements: Set by the French programme (French or English).

dates.deadlineNote: Students apply through a French institution, which sets its own internal deadline (example: Université Paris Cité accepted master's applications 12–29 Oct 2026 and PhD applications 12 Oct–2 Nov 2026). Institutions must submit applications to Campus France by 6 January 2027 (included); results are published from 12 April 2027.

procedure: Choose a French master's or PhD programme and apply for admission.
Ask the institution's international office whether it is nominating Eiffel candidates and what its internal deadline is.
Submit the Eiffel dossier through the institution's process.
Campus France publishes final results (from 12 April 2027 for this call, per Université Paris Cité).

sources.label: Campus France — France Excellence Eiffel scholarship program

verification.notes: Allowances, age limits and example dates checked against a participating university's official page. Each institution publishes its own process.

warnings: No direct applications to Campus France — only institutions can nominate.
The Eiffel allowance is not the same as a full tuition waiver.

title: Stipendium Hungaricum Scholarship
provider: Government of Hungary — Tempus Public Foundation
summary: Hungary's flagship government scholarship for students from partner countries, covering bachelor's, master's, one-tier master's, PhD and non-degree programmes at Hungarian universities.
eligibleNationalities: Citizens of Sending Partner countries. Applicants usually need nomination by their country's Sending Partner.
eligibleDisciplines: Programmes offered under the scheme by participating Hungarian universities.

coverage.tuition: Tuition-free education
coverage.stipend: Monthly stipend (amount set in the annual Call for Applications)
coverage.other: Student ID

eligibility: Citizen of a Sending Partner country
Meet the requirements in the Call for Applications for your study level
Meet the entry requirements of the chosen Hungarian programme
academicRequirements: Set by the chosen programme and the Call for Applications.
languageRequirements: Set by the chosen programme.

dates.deadlineNote: The 2026/27 deadline was 15 January 2026 (2 p.m. CET); the 2027/28 call has not been announced.

procedure: Read the Call for Applications and Application Guide for your level.
Check your country's Sending Partner and its nomination rules.
Apply through the official online application system.
Universities assess and may interview; final results are issued by Tempus Public Foundation.

verification.notes: Coverage and portal verified from the official 2026/27 announcement. The 2027/28 cycle dates are not yet confirmed.

warnings: Do not rely on the previous year's deadline — wait for the 2027/28 call.
Most applicants also need Sending Partner nomination.

title: Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Bursları)
provider: Presidency for Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB), Republic of Türkiye
summary: A government-funded, comprehensive scholarship for international students at Turkish universities, including university placement, a one-year Turkish language course, housing and a monthly stipend.
eligibleNationalities: International students of all nationalities (see official criteria).
eligibleDisciplines: Programmes available at participating Turkish universities.

coverage.tuition: Tuition fees covered
coverage.stipend: Monthly stipend: 6,500 TL (undergraduate), 9,500 TL (master's), 13,000 TL (PhD), as listed by YTB
coverage.travel: Flight ticket at the start of studies and on graduation
coverage.other: University and department placement; one-year Turkish language course

eligibility: Bachelor's: under 21 years of age
Master's: under 30 years of age
PhD: under 35 years of age
academicRequirements: Minimum 70% for bachelor's applicants; 75% for graduate applicants; 90% for Medicine, Dentistry and Pharmacy.
languageRequirements: Not specified by the official source checked; programmes may be taught in Turkish or English.

dates.deadlineNote: YTB's official calendar lists the general application period as 10 January – 20 February. The 2027 call has not been confirmed on this site yet.

procedure: Create an account and apply online through the official Türkiye Scholarships portal during the general application period.
Choose your preferred universities and programmes in the application.
Shortlisted candidates are invited to interviews.
Successful candidates are placed at a university by YTB.

verification.notes: Benefits, age limits and minimum grades verified on official YTB pages. 2027 dates await the official call.

warnings: Applying is free through the official portal — be cautious of anyone charging a fee to 'guarantee' selection.

title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) — Graduate Programs
provider: National Institute for International Education (NIIED), Ministry of Education, Republic of Korea
summary: Korean government scholarship for international master's, doctoral and research students, including a year of Korean language training. Pakistan received quota places in the 2026 round.
eligibleNationalities: Citizens of GKS partner countries listed in the annual guidelines (Pakistan had 8 Embassy-track and 17 University-track places in 2026).
eligibleDisciplines: Programmes offered by participating Korean universities.

coverage.tuition: Up to 5,000,000 KRW (admission fee covered by the university), per 2026 guidelines
coverage.stipend: 16,560,000 KRW per year during the degree programme (14,400,000 KRW per year during Korean language study); subject to budget
coverage.travel: Economy-class one-way airfare
coverage.insurance: Not specified by the source checked
coverage.other: Korean language training fees during the language year

eligibility: Under 40 years of age (born after 1 September 1986 for the 2026 round)
Citizen of an eligible country; neither applicant nor parents hold Korean citizenship
Hold (or expect) the prerequisite bachelor's or master's degree by the deadline in the guidelines
academicRequirements: Previous-degree CGPA of at least 80% (or top 20% of class), or equivalents such as 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0.
languageRequirements: Not required at application; TOPIK/English scores can add points (see guidelines).

dates.deadlineNote: In 2026 the Embassy-track online application ran 12–25 February 2026. The 2027 guidelines have not been confirmed on this site yet.

procedure: Choose a track: Embassy track (apply via the Korean embassy in your country) or University track (apply via a designated Korean university).
Prepare documents exactly as listed in the annual GKS guidelines.
Pass embassy/university screening, then NIIED's final selection.
Complete one year of Korean language training before the degree begins (unless exempt).

verification.notes: Figures taken from the official 2026 GKS-G guidelines document. Expect updates in the 2027 guidelines.

warnings: You may apply through only one track and one route in a given year.
Benefit amounts may change in the 2027 guidelines.

title: MEXT Japanese Government Scholarship — Research Students

eligibleDisciplines: Fields offered by Japanese universities, as defined in the guidelines.

coverage.tuition: Covered according to the MEXT guidelines
coverage.stipend: Monthly allowance (amount set in the annual guidelines)
coverage.travel: Airfare to Japan according to the guidelines

eligibility: Meet the age and degree conditions in the annual MEXT Research Student guidelines
Pass the embassy's document screening, written test and interview
academicRequirements: Set in the annual guidelines.
languageRequirements: Willingness to learn Japanese; programme-specific English or Japanese requirements.

dates.deadlineNote: For the 2027 intake, the Embassy of Japan in Pakistan's last date was 26 May 2026 and shortlisted candidates have been contacted. The 2028 call has not been confirmed.

procedure: Watch the Japanese embassy website for the annual call (usually spring).
Submit the printed application package to the embassy or consulate as instructed.
Shortlisted candidates take written tests and an interview.
Recommended candidates then secure acceptance from a Japanese university before MEXT's final decision.

sources.label: Embassy of Japan in Pakistan — MEXT Research Scholarship 2027

verification.notes: Pakistan application dates verified on the embassy page. Benefit amounts are not reproduced here — read the official guidelines.

warnings: The 2027 round in Pakistan is closed.
Application rules differ by embassy — always follow the embassy in your country of citizenship.

Any academic background except clinical medicine

Submit the online application through USEFP before the deadline.
Shortlisted applicants are tested and interviewed by USEFP.
Finalists are placed at U.S. universities.

verification.notes: Coverage, eligibility and deadline from USEFP's official announcement for the 2027 programme.

title: DAAD EPOS — Development-Related Postgraduate Courses
provider: German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD)
summary: DAAD scholarships for professionals from developing countries to take selected development-related master's (and some PhD) programmes at German universities.
eligibleNationalities: Nationals of developing countries on the OECD DAC list (Pakistan is on the DAC list).
eligibleDisciplines: Only the specific EPOS-listed courses (economics, engineering, environment, health, social sciences, governance and more).

coverage.tuition: Not specified by the source checked (many EPOS courses are tuition-free; check each course)
coverage.stipend: €992 per month for graduates; €1,300 per month for doctoral candidates (€1,400 from February 2026), as quoted for the 2027/28 call
coverage.travel: Travel allowance (unless covered by another source)
coverage.insurance: Health, accident and personal liability insurance

eligibility: National of a DAC-list developing country
Academic degree not older than six years at the time of application
At least two years of relevant professional experience after the bachelor's degree (internships and voluntary work usually do not count)
Above-average degree (upper third)
Have lived in Germany for no more than 15 months before applying
academicRequirements: Above-average degree (upper third) plus the admission criteria of the chosen course.
languageRequirements: Set by each course (English or German).

dates.deadlineNote: Deadlines differ for each course. Example: MSc Environmental Governance (University of Freiburg) — 15 October 2026.

procedure: Find an EPOS-listed course in the DAAD scholarship database.
Apply directly to the university course — it handles both admission and the scholarship pre-selection.
Follow the course's own deadline and document list.
DAAD makes the final scholarship decision based on course recommendations.

sources.label: University of Freiburg MEG — DAAD-EPOS scholarship

verification.notes: Rates and eligibility quoted from a course announcement of the 2027/28 call. Verify with the course and DAAD before applying.

warnings: You apply to the course, not to DAAD directly.
Professional experience is a strict requirement.

coverage.tuition: Programme participation costs covered for scholarship holders
coverage.stipend: Monthly allowance (€1,400 per month under current Erasmus+ rules — confirm on the programme page)
coverage.travel: Travel and installation contribution (amount depends on the programme rules)

eligibility: Hold a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) by the programme start
Meet the admission criteria of the specific programme
academicRequirements: Set by each programme consortium.
languageRequirements: Set by each programme (usually English).

Read each programme's eligibility rules and scholarship deadline.
Apply directly to each programme (up to three per year, per Erasmus Mundus rules).
Consortia rank applicants and award scholarships.

verification.notes: Programme structure from the official catalogue. Amounts and deadlines must be confirmed on each programme's website.

warnings: Scholarship conditions differ slightly between programmes — always read the programme's own rules.

eligibleDisciplines: Fee-paying English-taught bachelor's and master's programmes; rules differ by university.

University-specific criteria (often academic merit)

Apply as instructed by the university.

title: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships 2027/28
provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC)
summary: One-year master's study on an approved course at a participating UK university, jointly funded by the CSC and the university, for candidates from eligible low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries (including Pakistan) who could not otherwise afford UK study.
eligibleNationalities: Citizens of (or refugees in) 43 eligible Commonwealth countries who are permanently resident there, including Pakistan, Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and South Africa (full list on the CSC page).
eligibleDisciplines: Only the approved master's courses listed by the CSC, grouped under its six development themes (e.g. public health, data science and engineering for development, climate and crisis resilience, governance and peace).

coverage.tuition: Full approved tuition fees (covered by agreement between the CSC and the university)
coverage.stipend: £1,712 per month, or £2,000 per month at universities in the London metropolitan area (rates quoted by CSC at current levels)
coverage.travel: Approved return airfare between home country and the UK
coverage.other: Thesis grant where applicable; study travel grant; contribution to the mandatory visa TB test; child allowance for widowed, divorced or single-parent Scholars

eligibility: Be a citizen of, or have refugee status in, an eligible Commonwealth country
Be permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country
Be available to start UK study by September 2027
Not have studied or worked for one academic year or more in a high-income country
Be unable to afford UK study without the scholarship
Apply for an approved master's course at a participating UK university
academicRequirements: By September 2027, a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours, or a lower second-class degree plus a relevant postgraduate qualification (usually a master's).

dates.deadlineNote: CSC application closes 16:00 GMT on Tuesday 8 December 2026. Universities nominate selected candidates to the CSC in March 2027; check your university's own admission deadline.

procedure: Choose an approved course from the CSC's Commonwealth Shared Scholarships eligible-courses list.
Apply for admission to that master's course at the UK university, following its own rules and deadlines.
Submit the CSC application on CSC Central before 16:00 GMT on 8 December 2026, with all supporting documents.
The university nominates selected candidates to the CSC (March 2027); the CSC makes the final award.

sources.label: CSC — Commonwealth Shared Scholarships 2027 eligible courses

warnings: Only approved courses at participating UK universities are eligible.
